obligations.source_text: culture-library holds every repo's devague work as it evolves — specs, plans, delivery summaries, designs and the raw .devague state (frames, plans, deliveries, reviews, questions) — browsable and searchable by repo/project and by domain, with the artifact bytes kept in an S3 bucket

obligations.behavior: existing repodoc tests pass unchanged: same (repo, path, commit) re-push is a no-op, a new commit adds a version, visibility only tightens
obligations.source_text: Committed specs, plans and devague records already have a home: core/repodocs.py stores them as (repo, path) docs with one commit-pinned version per push (repodoc_versions), current = newest default-branch version, kind inferred from path prefix (docs/specs → spec, docs/plans → plan, docs/deliveries and .devague/ → devague-record), visibility failing closed

obligations.behavior: pushing the same (repo, path, commit) twice returns 200 and adds no row; a new commit adds exactly one version row
obligations.source_text: Reuse, don't replace, the repodocs identity and versioning model — (repo, path) identity, (repo, path, commit) dedup and the default-branch 'current' rule stay; the original spec's promises (docs/specs/2026-10-23-library-culture-dev.md lines 40-48) remain the contract this extends

obligations.behavior: two working pushes leave one draft holding the second content and zero new version rows; a later commit push adds one version and leaves the draft
obligations.source_text: Work-in-progress state is captured, not only committed state: a version can be pushed for uncommitted/working-tree content (e.g. a frame mid-/think, a plan mid-run) and for the gitignored .devague/reviews and .devague/questions, without fabricating a commit sha — today every version requires commit_sha matching a 40/64-hex regex

obligations.behavior: a gitignored review or question file pushed as working is stored and readable, with no commit sha required
obligations.source_text: Work-in-progress state is captured, not only committed state: a version can be pushed for uncommitted/working-tree content (e.g. a frame mid-/think, a plan mid-run) and for the gitignored .devague/reviews and .devague/questions, without fabricating a commit sha — today every version requires commit_sha matching a 40/64-hex regex

obligations.behavior: domain=X returns only docs of projects declaring X; project=P&connected=1 adds only P's declared connections; an unknown domain returns an empty list, not an error
obligations.source_text: Repo documents carry project and domain scope: the project is the repo, its domains come from the repo's culture.yaml (pushed by culture-rules), and projects can declare connections to other projects; documents can be listed and filtered by project (including connected projects) and by domain through the API, the MCP tools and the site

obligations.behavior: a push carrying new domains for a repo replaces that project's domains; documents of the repo are re-scoped without re-pushing them
obligations.source_text: Repo documents carry project and domain scope: the project is the repo, its domains come from the repo's culture.yaml (pushed by culture-rules), and projects can declare connections to other projects; documents can be listed and filtered by project (including connected projects) and by domain through the API, the MCP tools and the site

obligations.behavior: a version write produces object key <repo>/<path>@<commit> (draft: @working) with the pushed bytes and content-type; the local blob is still written first
obligations.source_text: Every repo document version is written through to an AWS S3 bucket as a human-readable mirror tree — committed versions at `<repo>/<path>@<commit>`, the working draft at `<repo>/<path>@working` — behind a storage interface; the local content-addressed blob store stays the library's primary copy and backup source

obligations.behavior: base dependencies stay [], the S3 client package is in its own optional extra, importing culture_library.cli with it blocked succeeds, and no module under core/ imports a network library
obligations.source_text: core/ stays stdlib-only and network-free and base dependencies stay empty: any S3 client is an optional extra imported lazily outside core/, behind a protocol core/ defines

obligations.behavior: a PNG and an HTML prototype round-trip byte-identical; the site shows the image inline and the HTML as a downloadable/sandboxed view, never executed in the library origin
obligations.source_text: Designs are a supported artifact: design docs with their binary assets (screenshots, HTML prototypes, images) — e.g. this repo's docs/design/library-site.md, prototype.html and 30 reference screenshots — can be stored and viewed, not only UTF-8 text

obligations.behavior: a phrase only in a spec body returns that doc with source=repodoc; a key without private access gets zero repodoc hits
obligations.source_text: Specs, plans, deliveries and devague records are searchable (full-text and RAG) with the same visibility rule as items, closing issue #4

obligations.seam: indexer text extractor for devague JSON
obligations.behavior: a frame's indexed text contains every claim text and honesty condition text; no chunk consists only of JSON punctuation or keys
obligations.source_text: Indexing devague JSON goes through a JSON-aware text extractor (claims, honesty conditions, tasks, risks as prose), not the raw pretty-printed JSON

obligations.behavior: a parity test fails if a repodoc route has no tool or a tool has no route
obligations.source_text: Agents get MCP tools for repo documents (list by repo/project/domain, read current or a version, push, search) mirroring the HTTP routes one to one, like EVAL_ROUTES

obligations.behavior: each new version or draft overwrite appends exactly one event carrying repo, path and commit-or-working; a no-op re-push appends none
obligations.source_text: A repo document change emits a feed event so subscribers (culture-rules, agents) can react to a spec or plan update

obligations.behavior: every delivery JSON under ~/git top-level repos renders without the raw fallback; review/question markdown renders as Markdown
obligations.source_text: Delivery JSON, reviews and questions render as readable pages like frames and plans do

obligations.behavior: the site lists projects and domains; a project page groups each slug's spec, plan, delivery and frame, and shows connected projects
obligations.source_text: The site gets a browse view by repo/project and by domain, with a spec's linked plan, delivery and frame shown together (joined on devague slug)

obligations.behavior: no subprocess, git or devague invocation exists anywhere in culture_library, including the new storage and S3 code
obligations.source_text: The library only receives pushed content: nothing in culture_library runs git or devague; the collector that reads repos and .devague dirs lives outside this package (a culture-rules rule, a devague hook, or a separate client)

obligations.seam: push from a repo and from its worktree
obligations.behavior: the same (remote, path, commit) from two checkout paths yields one doc and one version
obligations.source_text: Git worktree copies (.worktrees.*/, *-worktrees/) never multiply documents: dedup stays on (repo, path, commit) and working-state pushes are keyed by repo, not by checkout path

obligations.seam: repodoc visibility at push + S3 reads
obligations.behavior: every pushed doc lands private whatever the request says; a read key without private access sees none; S3 bytes are only reachable through the library
obligations.source_text: Migrated documents are private: every repo document pushed by culture-rules lands private regardless of the repo's GitHub visibility (decision c31), and the S3 bucket is never publicly readable — bytes reach readers only through the library's visibility check

obligations.behavior: for each sampled repo file the sha256 equals the library current/draft sha256 and the S3 object's sha256; the report lists 0 missing and 0 mismatched
obligations.source_text: For at least 5 sampled repos, 100% of committed docs/{specs,plans,deliveries}/*.md, docs/design/** and .devague/** files pushed by culture-rules appear in the library and in S3 with sha256 matching the repo file

obligations.behavior: a frame edit shows up as the draft within one cycle; repodoc_versions row count for that doc is unchanged
obligations.source_text: A working-draft edit to a frame reaches the library within 1 culture-rules cycle and replaces the previous draft without adding a version (versions count unchanged, draft sha256 updated)

obligations.seam: filter API, MCP tool and site with 3 projects in 2 domains
obligations.behavior: each filter returns exactly the expected document set in all three surfaces, and 0 documents from other repos
obligations.source_text: Filtering by one domain or one project (with connected projects) returns exactly the documents of the repos declaring it — 0 from others — in the API, MCP and site

obligations.behavior: the filed issue links this spec and states endpoints, payload fields (repo, path, commit-or-working, bytes, domains, connected, spec links, tombstones), worktree exclusion and the all-private rule
obligations.source_text: culture-rules receives the push contract as a sibling-repo issue (via the communicate skill): endpoints, payload (repo, path, commit or working, content bytes, culture.yaml domains/connected), worktree exclusion and the all-private rule

obligations.seam: push payload spec links + spec view
obligations.behavior: a delivered spec shows its PR and merge commit; after a later commit renames an implementing file, the spec's code links show the new path; a Spec: trailer commit is linked even if it touches files outside the merge diff
obligations.source_text: A spec is tied to the repo and commits that realize it: first to the merge that delivered it (repo, PR, merge commit), and later to the code that currently represents it — the link follows the implementing code forward as it changes, rather than freezing at the merge (operator, 2026-10-30)

obligations.behavior: a tombstone hides the doc from current listings at that commit, keeps its history readable, discards its draft, and deletes nothing in S3
obligations.source_text: Deletions propagate: when a file disappears from a repo (git rm, a deleted frame, a never-committed draft discarded), culture-rules sends a tombstone; the library marks the doc removed at that commit (history kept, hidden from current lists) and drops a stale working draft — nothing is deleted from S3

obligations.behavior: with the S3 backend failing, pushes return 2xx and the outbox grows; /api/status reports pending count and oldest age; after recovery a reconcile leaves 0 pending
obligations.source_text: S3 mirroring runs from a durable outbox table (doc version, key, state, attempts, last error) drained outside the push request; a reconcile verb re-mirrors anything missing, and /api/status reports mirror lag and failures

obligations.seam: deploy check against the AWS bucket
obligations.behavior: the check fails if Block Public Access, default encryption or versioning is off, or the library's credentials can call DeleteObject
obligations.source_text: The bucket is private and append-only from the library's side: Block Public Access on, SSE encryption on, S3 Versioning on (so @working overwrites keep prior bytes), and the library's IAM credentials allow only PutObject/GetObject/ListBucket on that one bucket — no DeleteObject

obligations.seam: items kind CHECK rebuild + key kinds allow-list
obligations.behavior: first open after upgrade accepts kind design with row counts unchanged; the culture-rules key can write spec, plan, devague-record and design and is refused book
obligations.source_text: A design kind is added (docs/design/** and binary assets under the other prefixes), widening KINDS — so the items kind CHECK rebuild runs once on first open — and the culture-rules push key is a write key scoped to kinds spec, plan, devague-record, design

obligations.behavior: a 1.3 MB binary round-trips; a body over the configured limit gets 413 with a structured code and stores nothing
obligations.source_text: Repo document pushes accept binary content (multipart or base64) up to a configured size limit like UPLOAD_LIMITS, refusing larger files with a structured 413; the largest file in the corpus today is 1.3 MB

obligations.behavior: with 4,000+ repodocs queued, a newly uploaded library item is indexed before them; a gateway outage pauses and then resumes the backfill without losing queued work
obligations.source_text: The initial backfill indexes through the existing index queue at low priority so it never starves item indexing or the gateway: about 4,600 files at roughly 13-22 chunks/s for gemma2-embed is tens of minutes of embedding, not one burst

obligations.behavior: without a source filter, retrieval returns library items only; eval runs store the source filter; eval set 1 retrieves the same ids before and after the corpus is indexed
obligations.source_text: Adding repo documents to search does not move the existing eval baseline: /api/rag/retrieve keeps returning library items only unless a caller opts into repodocs (source filter), and eval runs record that filter in their retrieval config

obligations.behavior: a read key without private access lists 0 migrated docs; a private-access key lists them all; the runbook names each client's key and whether it has private access
obligations.source_text: Agents that should read the migrated corpus hold keys with private access (all docs are private, c31); a shared read-only key without private access sees none of it, and this is documented per client (Gwen, xteink, culture-rules, mesh MCP)

obligations.behavior: the GitHub-removal plan includes a full-corpus verify task (every repo, every file) that must pass before any file is removed
obligations.source_text: Removing documents from GitHub (follow-up v2) is gated on a full-corpus verification across every repo — sha256 of each repo file equals library and S3 — not on the 5-repo sample of c36

obligations.behavior: backup covers draft blobs and the outbox; restoring onto an empty data dir restores drafts and pending outbox rows with S3 unreachable
obligations.source_text: S3 is a mirror, not the backup: culture-library backup keeps working from the local blob store, now also covering working drafts and the outbox (any new table with sha256 is picked up automatically)

obligations.behavior: a version write produces object key `<repo>/<path>@<commit>` (draft: `@working`) with the pushed bytes and content-type; the local blob is still written first
obligations.source_text: Every repo document version is written through to an AWS S3 bucket as a human-readable mirror tree — committed versions at `<repo>/<path>@<commit>`, the working draft at `<repo>/<path>@working` — behind a storage interface; the local content-addressed blob store stays the library's primary copy and backup source
